methodological_rigor.justification: This multi-institutional retrospective study of 75 urachal carcinoma cases uses appropriate statistical methods including Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, log-rank testing, and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression to identify independent prognostic factors. The inclusion of two senior pathologists for diagnostic consistency and the use of a combined BC Cancer/MD Anderson database strengthens the analysis. Limitations include heterogeneous staging assessment (TURBT vs. cystectomy specimens precluding uniform pT staging), variable IHC availability across cases, and the extended study period (1989–2023) introducing treatment heterogeneity. The 5-year CSS difference (39% vs. 64%) did not reach statistical significance (p=0.053), yet multivariate analysis confirms independent prognostic significance.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective multi-institutional case series (LoE 4) addressing an extremely rare malignancy where even 28 SRCC cases represents one of the largest published series. The establishment of SRCC morphology as an independent predictor of OS (HR=3.38) and CSS (HR=3.15) has direct clinical implications for staging workup, counseling, and treatment planning. The study supports classification of urachal SRCC as a distinct clinical entity warranting dedicated therapeutic strategies, which is directly actionable for pathologists and urologists.

reporting_quality.justification: The study follows observational reporting conventions reasonably well with clear eligibility criteria, histological definitions, IHC methodology, and statistical approaches described. Survival curves and HR with 95% CI are reported. However, IHC was only available for subsets of patients (varying denominators across markers), limiting systematic profiling. MMR data were available for only 3/75 patients. No public data repository deposit is mentioned. The extended study period introduces unstandardized treatment protocols across cases.

novelty_literature.justification: This study provides one of the largest published multi-institutional series of urachal SRCC (n=28), significantly expanding available literature on an extremely rare entity previously limited to case reports and very small series. The multivariate confirmation of SRCC morphology as an independent adverse prognostic factor, the IHC profiling data (CK20/CDX2/SATB2 expression patterns), and the direct comparison against non-SRCC urachal carcinomas represent a meaningful advance beyond prior single-case and small-series reports in this poorly characterized disease.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is adequately written with appropriate structure and reporting of clinicopathological findings. Tables effectively present comparative data. The discussion contextualizes findings against the sparse literature and addresses diagnostic challenges and treatment approaches. Some sections could benefit from tightening, particularly the IHC discussion which covers established diagnostic markers with limited new insights. The conclusions are proportionate but somewhat broad given the limitations of the dataset.

key_strengths: Largest published multi-institutional series of urachal SRCC (n=28), providing meaningful epidemiological and prognostic data for an extremely rare entity previously limited to case reports
Multivariate Cox regression confirming SRCC morphology as independent predictor of both OS (HR=3.38) and CSS (HR=3.15), establishing clinical significance beyond descriptive characterization
Dual senior pathologist review at two major cancer centers (BC Cancer and MD Anderson) ensuring diagnostic consistency
IHC profiling data (CK20 86%, CDX2 89%, SATB2 100%) provides practical diagnostic reference for this challenging entity
key_concerns: Heterogeneous staging assessment due to reliance on TURBT vs. cystectomy specimens prevented uniform pT staging across the entire cohort
Extended 34-year study period (1989-2023) encompasses major changes in chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and surgical technique, introducing substantial treatment heterogeneity
MMR/MSI status assessed in only 3/75 patients despite potential actionability for immunotherapy; IHC marker availability was highly variable across cases
5-year CSS difference (39% vs. 64%, p=0.053) did not reach statistical significance, undermining the CSS-specific conclusions in the abstract
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is the largest multi-institutional series on urachal SRCC and provides genuinely novel prognostic data for an extremely rare entity; Tier 3 is appropriate given the inherent limitations of retrospective case series for rare diseases and the incomplete molecular characterization. Minor revisions should address the non-significant CSS p-value in the abstract and expand MSI/MMR testing discussion given therapeutic implications.
